proof_summary: Counting pairs divisible by each power of \(p\) gives the numerator valuation \(\sum_{i\ge1}\lfloor m/p^i\rfloor^2\), while Legendre’s formula gives the denominator valuation \(\sum_{i\ge1}\sum_k k\lfloor m/(kp^i)\rfloor\); the bound \(\sum_{k\le M}k\lfloor M/k\rfloor\le M^2\) establishes exact divisibility. If \(p\nmid m+1\), the newly added gcd row and column contribute no \(p\)-factor and all relevant factorial-floor valuations remain unchanged, so iterating this one-step invariance from \(np\) through the next \(p-1\) positions proves the result.
